issues.description: @Deprecated annotation dropped from legacy formats while making them read-only — signal direction is wrong
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat lose @Deprecated in this patch. A read-only legacy codec that throws on write is more deprecated than before, not less. Restore @Deprecated (ideally with forRemoval and since= pointing at Lucene104) so downstream consumers get compiler-level migration signal.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException without naming the replacement format
issues.detail: Both formats throw 'Old codecs may only be used for reading' with no migration pointer. The exception message should name Lucene104HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat so the stack trace is itself the migration doc. Cheap fix, high payoff for the operator hitting this on a rolling upgrade at 2am.

issues.description: Public API symbols quietly demoted to package-private without a deprecation cycle
issues.detail: NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval, rawVectorFormat, OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues.load, and the reader class flip from public to package-private in the same patch that moves packages. Downstream importers get a hard compile break with no grace period. Either keep them public in the new package or land visibility tightening as a separate, announced patch.

issues.description: Writer capability re-attached via test-only RW subclasses defeats the read-only separation
issues.detail: Moving formats to backward-codecs should mean read-only, but RW subclasses reintroduce writing by overriding fieldsWriter and sharing package-private state. The read/write identity is smeared across base and test subclass. Cleaner: backward type exposes only the reader path; throwing at runtime is the easy fix, not the simple one.

issues.description: protected fields downgraded to package-private on a public abstract class
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues fields move from protected to package-private on a public abstract class. Any external subclass — which is the whole point of protected — silently loses access. Either document that subclassing outside the package is no longer supported, or revert to protected.

issues.description: Move is partial — Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer remains in core
issues.detail: The author admits the scorer cannot move yet, leaving the 'legacy = backward_codecs' identity as a half-truth: most pieces live in backward_codecs.lucene99, but core still depends on lucene99 quantization machinery. Acceptable as interim, but the follow-up needs a tracked issue and a Javadoc note on the format naming the remaining dependency.

synthesis.summary: The package move to backward_codecs is the right direction, but the patch bundles three independent changes — relocation, visibility tightening, and writer disablement — making it hostile to bisect and to downstream consumers. The panel agrees the most actionable fixes are restoring @Deprecated, naming the replacement format (Lucene104) in the UnsupportedOperationException message, and either preserving public visibility in the new package or splitting the visibility shrink into a separate announced patch. Re-attaching writer capability via test-only RW subclasses partially undoes the read-only separation the move was meant to establish. The remaining Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer in core leaves the decomposition half-done and should be tracked explicitly. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — correct direction, thin on migration signal and surgical separation.
